narration.text: Finding an entity is easy when you know its name.
A search of entity names can take us directly to the entity we seek.

caption: The entity exists. The name does not match.

narration.text: But what if the text calls him something else?
The man in the dinner jacket.
A search of names and aliases may find nothing.
Yet across a corpus, an entity may be referred to in many different ways.
Each annotated mention connects a particular textual occurrence to its referent.
Instead of searching the names of entities, we can search the language used to refer to them.
Follow a matching mention, and we arrive at the entity itself.
Two mentions of Bond lead to one person.
The same expression may even lead to different entities. The recorded associations, rather than the words alone, determine the results.
And every result retains a connection to the passage from which it was discovered.

caption: The language of a corpus becomes an index into its knowledge graph.

narration.text: The language of a corpus becomes an index into its knowledge graph.
